title: The Only Place You Could Go Outside Without a Spacesuit
topic: Titan: thick nitrogen air at about 1.5x Earth pressure, no oxygen, -179 C, 14% gravity, human-powered flight, slow methane rain, methane lakes

beats.narration: There's one place in the solar system where you could step outside without a spacesuit. It's Titan, Saturn's biggest moon.
phrases: There's one place in the solar system

beats.narration: On the Moon or Mars, you'd need a pressure suit. But Titan's air is so thick, it presses on you about one and a half times harder than Earth's. Heavy, but safe.
phrases: But Titan's air is so thick,
one and a half times harder than Earth's.

beats.narration: There's a catch. That air is mostly nitrogen, with no oxygen at all. So you'd still need a mask.
phrases: So you'd still need a mask.

beats.narration: And it's minus one hundred seventy-nine degrees Celsius. So add the warmest coat ever made.
phrases: So add the warmest coat ever made.

beats.narration: Now the fun part. Gravity here is only fourteen percent of Earth's. With air this thick, you could strap wings to your arms, flap, and actually fly.
phrases: you could strap wings to your arms,

beats.narration: Even the rain is strange. It's liquid methane, falling about five times slower than rain on Earth.
It fills lakes bigger than any of the Great Lakes. Just don't go swimming. Methane is so light, you'd sink straight to the bottom.
phrases: than any of the Great Lakes.
you'd sink straight to the bottom.

beats.narration: So, Titan. No spacesuit needed. Just bring a mask, a coat, and wings.
